function.mechanism: Hydrates and binds water to increase viscosity and stabilize/emulsify dispersed food systems.

adi.basis: 2017 EFSA re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for the general population at refined exposure.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA 2024 follow-up found submitted data insufficient to support safe use in infants/young children in FC 13.1.1, 13.1.5.1, and 13.1.5.2; 2017 finding of no general-population safety concern remains for reported uses.

concerns.summary: EFSA 2024 concluded data were insufficient to demonstrate safe use for infants/young children in specific medical and formula categories (FC 13.1.1, 13.1.5.1, 13.1.5.2).
Hypersensitivity risk is linked to residual proteinaceous material; EFSA discussed case-report context and recommended minimizing allergenic impurities.
Severe choking/esophageal obstruction has been reported in dry bolus hydrocolloid contexts (including guar gum), reflected in regulatory warning context for hydrophilic gums.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no adverse effects reported in subchronic and carcinogenicity studies at highest tested doses in reviewed dataset.
EFSA 2017: no need for numerical ADI and no general-population safety concern at refined exposure.
Recent clinical studies/meta-analyses generally report tolerability in studied adult populations (e.g., PHGG enteral formula RCT; metabolic RCT/meta-analyses).

populations: infants and young children consuming special medical foods
adi_exceedance.notes: Classical ADI exceedance is not applicable because EFSA/JECFA did not set a numerical ADI. Risk focus is on population-specific uncertainty (infants/young children in specific categories), not ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: General-population evidence supports low concern under approved uses, but EFSA's latest follow-up could not establish safety for specific infant/young-child categories and highlighted specification/impurity issues.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 no numerical ADI and no general-population safety concern
EFSA 2024 insufficient data for infant/young-child special categories
FDA GRAS with defined CFR use conditions
No IARC monograph classification for guar gum found
